NACE is a suitable separation technique for the analysis of the metabolites of harma‐ ne.
NACE‐MS and RP‐HPC‐MS were used in combination to study the metabolism of the monoaminooxide inhibitor harmane.
NACE is an excellent separation technique to support metabolite identification studies of drugs and that the combination of NACE and RP HPLC is superior to the use of either technique alone.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new methods for the detection and identification of drug metabolites.
a new approach to the study of the metabolism of harmane.
the development of a novel analytical method for metabolism studies of harmaine, which is based on the combination of NACE, EC, and mass spectrometric detection (NACE‐EC‐ESI‐MS).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the combination of both NCE and HPLC provides a better overview of the metabolism than either of them alone.
HPLC is superior to NACE for the separation of harmane metabolites, but NACE is a valuable additional technique to gain further information about metabolites.
the combination of NACE, EC, and ESI MS is an excellent tool to study metabolic processes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
NACE is a useful tool in metabolism studies, especially in combination with HPLC.
NACE‐MS can be used as an alternative separation technique in metabolism study to HPLC, since it is able to separate polar compounds.
the combination of EC and NACE‐MS is able to deliver additional information about possible metabolic pathways and products of harmane compared to HPLCEC‐MS and NACE‐EC‐MS alone.
The main takeaway from our work is that
NACE can be used in metabolism studies to support HPLC.

NACE is able, in combination with EC and MS, to detect metabolites that are not detectable with HPLC, which can lead to the discovery of metabolites that were previously unknown and, thus, can lead to the improvement of drug development.
the combination of NACE and HPLC‐EC‐MS/MS is a powerful technique to study the metabolism of drugs and to support the development of new drugs.
